solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Our close relatives guzzle fruit cups

indicators.note: to cup something is to hold it in the hollow of a hand, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: a fruit growing in bunches
to guzzle is to eat greedily

explanation.surface: Someone describes a family member gobbling down fruit cups at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cups' looks like a noun after 'fruit', but it is a verb: the fruit holds the guzzling inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimpanzees and orangutans are the primates most closely related to humans, our nearest cousins in evolution.

clue.text: What unequipped traveller has, up in African country

indicators.note: in a down entry, going up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: someone travelling unequipped has no bag

explanation.surface: A backpacker without gear arrives in an African country.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is a riddle: what does a traveller with no equipment have? No bag.
explanation.definitionFit: Gabon is a nation on the Atlantic coast of central Africa, straddling the equator.

clue.text: Requisite messages sent? I already received this

indicators.note: what is received is held inside, so the letters sit within the run of words

parts.note: letters running across the word boundaries of messages sent I already

explanation.surface: Someone told about vital messages being sent says they already have them.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters start inside 'messages' and end inside 'already'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something requisite is required or indispensable, the same sense as essential as an adjective.

clue.text: Drier river crossed by the bank nearest to us

indicators.note: a thing crossed by another has it lying across it, here with one letter set inside the word

parts.note: this, as against that, points to the nearer thing
R is the map abbreviation for river
a bank of seats or oars is a tier or row

explanation.surface: A river is crossed by the nearer riverbank, which is drier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bank nearest to us' reads as one riverbank, but it splits into two words, and 'bank' means a row, not a shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Being thirstier is being more in need of a drink, so in the comparative sense of drier as more parched.

clue.text: Twice supporting chief on crime, defending Old Bill

indicators.note: a defender stands round what it guards, so one piece is placed inside another

parts.note: two words for in favour of: pro and for
chief means principal, main
vice is immoral or criminal activity
O is the standard abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: A police backer supports the chief in fighting crime and defending the force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Bill' is British slang for the police, a decoy here: Old gives O and Bill is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro forma invoice is a preliminary bill sent before goods are supplied, stating what will be charged.

clue.text: Poultryman fails badly with rising costs and low investment

definitions.text: with rising costs and low investment

indicators.note: something done badly is botched and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A chicken farmer's business collapses as costs rise and nobody invests.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumpflation is economic stagnation combined with inflation, so the adjective describes rising prices amid falling investment.

clue.text: Devout Jew is able to prove who he is

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a member of a strictly observant Jewish movement

definitions.text: is able to prove who he is
definitions.meaning: second meaning, split in two: possesses identification

explanation.surface: A religious man can show papers proving his identity.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer as HAS ID: someone carrying identification can prove who he is.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hasid is a follower of Hasidism, a pious Orthodox Jewish movement founded in eighteenth-century Poland.

clue.text: At intervals, they appear very excited

indicators.note: taking things at intervals means every other one, skipping those in between

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: Every so often they show up in a state of great excitement.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyper is informal for overexcited or hyperactive, unable to keep still.

clue.text: The Times keeping cool about confused situation

indicators.note: turning about means facing the other way, so the whole is read backwards
to keep something is to hold it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a newspaper refers to itself as we and us
a fan cools you

explanation.surface: The newspaper keeps a level head amid a muddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Times' here is the paper speaking of itself, as setters in it often do: US.
explanation.definitionFit: Snafu is military slang, an acronym for a situation in total chaos, a muddle or mess-up.

clue.text: Face feverish Cockney in debate

indicators.note: Cockney speakers drop the H at the start of words, so that letter goes

parts.note: a dial is the face of a clock, or slang for a person's face
hectic once meant feverish, as in a hectic flush

explanation.surface: A flushed East Londoner squares up in an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is a working-class Londoner, whose accent drops initial H.
explanation.definitionFit: Dialectic is the art of reaching truth through reasoned argument and counter-argument, a formal kind of discussion.

clue.text: Code of conduct in transport concealed nothing

parts.note: a bus is public transport
past tense of hide
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A rule about passengers hiding nothing on public transport.
explanation.definitionFit: Bushido is the samurai's ethical code in feudal Japan, stressing loyalty, honour and courage.

clue.text: City, you said very softly, sadly going backwards

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so the letter written is the one that sounds like the word

parts.note: the letter U is pronounced like the word you
pianissimo, the musical marking for very soft

indicators.note: moving backwards means the letters run right to left

parts.note: alas is an exclamation of sorrow

explanation.surface: Someone murmured sadly as they left a city behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sadly' looks like an adverb but stands for the word alas.
explanation.definitionFit: Uppsala is a university city in Sweden, north of Stockholm.

clue.text: Dates in Rome — November 1 and 1st of September

parts.note: N is November in the radio alphabet
the numeral spelt out

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter alone

parts.note: the opening letter of the month

explanation.surface: A list of Roman dates: the first of November and the first of September.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient Roman calendar the nones were the ninth day before the ides, the 5th or 7th of each month.

clue.text: Suitable mate with right air

parts.note: oppo is British slang for a friend or colleague
R abbreviates right
an air is a melody

explanation.surface: A fitting partner who also carries himself correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: Opportune means well-timed or appropriate to the occasion, suitable for the purpose.

clue.text: Breathe aloud, whenever retreating in fantasy

indicators.note: spoken out loud, so letters are chosen for sound, not spelling

parts.note: to sigh is to breathe out audibly; the abbreviation for science is said the same

indicators.note: a retreating army goes back the way it came, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: if can mean whenever, as in 'if it rains, we stay in'

explanation.surface: Someone breathes noisily whenever they back away inside a dream world.
explanation.walkthrough: The short form of science is pronounced like sigh.
explanation.definitionFit: Science fiction is a genre of imaginative storytelling, and the fantasy shelf in a bookshop often shares space with it.

clue.text: Do — but not does?

parts.note: surface reading: a verb and its third-person form, as if querying grammar
setter's reading: a do is a party, and does are female deer, so this party is for males only, the night before a wedding

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'does' as female deer, not the verb: a party where only the males (stags) are invited.
explanation.definitionFit: A pre-wedding celebration for the groom and his male friends; in deer terms the males are stags and females does.

clue.text: Is it one 100,000th of a dollar for this girl?

definitions.text: Is it one 100,000th of a dollar
definitions.meaning: first meaning, read jokingly: a thousandth of a cent, there being a hundred cents to the dollar
second meaning: a female first name

explanation.walkthrough: The metric prefix milli means a thousandth, so a thousandth of a cent is one hundred-thousandth of a dollar.
explanation.definitionFit: Millicent is a traditional female given name, so it names this girl.

clue.text: Cover placed around good books? One's revolting

indicators.note: something placed around another surrounds it, so one letter sits inside the word

parts.note: to insure is to provide cover against loss
G abbreviates good
the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A disgusted reader finds a dust jacket wrapped around supposedly good books.
explanation.walkthrough: 'good books' reads as a phrase but splits: good gives G and books the New Testament. 'revolting' means rebelling, not disgusting.
explanation.definitionFit: An insurgent is a rebel rising against authority, someone who revolts.

clue.text: Mysterious items drunkard brought in front of Edward Heath

indicators.note: something brought in goes inside, so the drunkard is set within the other letters

parts.note: Erica is the botanical genus of heaths and heathers
a sot is a habitual drunk

indicators.note: the front of a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: the opening letter of the name

explanation.surface: A drunk is brought before the former British Prime Minister Edward Heath, with some odd items.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a British Prime Minister in the 1970s; here his name splits into a first letter and a plant genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoterica are obscure or arcane things understood only by a few, so items with mystery about them.

clue.text: Doctor to go for the French meat

parts.note: aller is French for the verb to go
the meat of an argument is its substance, its gist

explanation.surface: A doctor tells you to choose French meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go for' looks like 'choose', but 'for the French' means 'in French'.
explanation.definitionFit: An allergist is a physician who specialises in diagnosing and treating allergies.

clue.text: Closed in thus, refusing to complain

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: Latin sic, thus, used to flag a quoted error
a door pushed to is closed

explanation.surface: Shut away like this, someone refuses to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person endures hardship without showing feelings or protesting, named after the Greek philosophical school.

clue.text: Pal, very excited, loves chat in foreign language

indicators.note: excited letters are stirred up and moved about into a new order

parts.note: the letters to rearrange
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O; two of them

explanation.surface: An eager friend loves chatting away in another tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: Parleyvoo is a jokey English spelling of the French 'parlez-vous'.
explanation.definitionFit: To parleyvoo is humorous slang for speaking French, from the question 'parlez-vous français?'

clue.text: Show gun use is heartless

parts.note: to gun an engine is to rev it

indicators.note: without its heart a word loses its middle, keeping only the ends

parts.note: the end letters of the word

explanation.surface: A display of gun use is said to be cruel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gun' looks like a weapon but is a verb meaning to race an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A revue is a theatrical show of sketches, songs and dances, often satirical.

clue.text: Case of elder wine was off

indicators.note: a case is the outside shell, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters
red is a kind of wine

explanation.surface: A crate of elderflower wine had gone bad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of elder wine' reads as a crate of elderberry wine, but case means only the outside letters of elder.
explanation.definitionFit: To be off is to be mistaken or wide of the mark, so erred, made an error, matches 'was off'.

clue.text: Discharge ambassador with funny clothing

indicators.note: clothing wraps round a body, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: rum is British for odd or peculiar
His Excellency, the title of an ambassador

explanation.surface: An envoy in silly clothes is dismissed from his post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a verb for sacking, but it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is watery mucus discharged from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Habits of a Utopian

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the customs and conventions of a society
second meaning, split with an apostrophe: belonging to Thomas More, author of Utopia

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Thomas More wrote Utopia (1516), so his possessive, More's, means 'of a Utopian'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mores are the customs and moral conventions of a community, its characteristic habits.

clue.text: Almost defeat this person in board game

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a reverse is a setback or defeat
the setter refers to themself

explanation.surface: Someone nearly loses at a board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Reversi is a two-player game on an eight-by-eight grid, also sold as Othello, where captured counters are flipped.

clue.text: Stone removed from grander workshop

indicators.note: taking something out of a word leaves the rest behind

parts.note: more stately, grander
st is the abbreviation for stone, a British weight of fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A stone is taken out of a grander building to make a workshop.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's studio, a workroom.

clue.text: Heard why competitors, losing the lead, give in

indicators.note: the lead is the front, so the opening letter goes
what is heard is spoken, so the letter used sounds like the word

parts.note: the letter Y is pronounced like why
the field is everyone in a race

explanation.surface: Someone asks why the racers who fall behind surrender.
explanation.definitionFit: To yield is to surrender or submit, the same as giving in.

clue.text: Abroad, get in spa with last of yummy mummies?

indicators.note: abroad can mean astray or all over the place, so these letters wander out of order

parts.note: letters to rearrange

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: final letter

explanation.surface: Glamorous young mothers head to a spa abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yummy mummies' (stylish young mothers) is a red herring: the question mark flags mummies as examples of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous embalmed mummies came from ancient Egypt, so they are Egyptians, a definition by example.
